messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Help with open issues on github.
parts:
Hi all,

I could really use your help. There are way too many open issues on our repos and I really want it to be cut down to something reasonable.

Here is our current status:
- Stan: 218 open issues. https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues
- Stan Math: 112 open issues. https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues

If you have any time to spare, please help out. You don't have to be coder. You can do this with any 15 mins.

1. Go to either the Stan issues (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues) or Math issues (https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues) on GitHub. Log in.
2. Go to any page of the issues (preferably something older, but anywhere is good). Click on any issue. It'll look like this: https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/61
3. Take some action:
  - Read the issue.
  - If it's irrelevant now, please close the issue! That's the best thing to do.
  - If it's still relevant, add tags to the issue if there aren't any. Write a comment that you've seen it. Assign someone. Do something with it. Ask a question. In other words, don't just read it and let it go.

Thanks. Please help out if you have a few minutes. It would make me feel a lot better about the stability of our project if the number of issues were manageable.


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Help with open issues on github.
parts:
We have the "future" milestone already.

I think we should keep the longer-term goal wiki.

I'd very much like to restrict the issue tracker to:

* concrete feature requests with a functional spec
in the form of a basic interface design

* bug reports (should these be required to be reproducible
before allowed to stand?)

That will keep the issues narrowly scoped and still allow us
to have bigger design discussions on the outside.

- Bob

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Help with open issues on github.
parts:
I think the solution here is to mark as outdated (or delete) any wiki
pages which are out of date. Github doesn't make this kind of
housekeeping as easy as it should be.

p.s. there are features in Discourse which would make wiki pages
unnecessary, see https://www.discourse.org/about/ ("Wiki posts").
Basically you can have a long-running discussion thread which has wiki
features. Since everything in a discussion thread is dated, it's very
easy to see whether or not something is out of date.
